sources: Harbison, Peter. *Pre-Christian Ireland: From the First Settlers to the Early Celts*. London: Thames and Hudson, 1988, 47.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The court tomb is a mythological site. It is one of the early burial structures built by the pre-Celtic megalithic peoples across the Celtic lands. A paved, half-circle court stands before a stone pile that covers a small inner chamber whose door faces east. The court at the great tomb of Creevykeel in County Sligo, Ireland, could hold about 50 people. If these mounds were true graves, the courts may have been the ground for rites of burial.
